narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated a 77.4% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That is a high-risk estimate, not a certainty, and it is the reason your application was treated as too risky to advance.

The strongest factor was your third-year class-rank decile: you are in the second decile, while accepted students average around the sixth. This placed you well below the admitted profile and pushed the prediction most strongly toward failure. Your LSAT score of 43 was the second most influential factor; because it is above the accepted average of about 37, it actually pushed toward passing and worked in your favor. However, it was not enough to offset the academic concerns. The third most important factor was your first-year class-rank decile, also 2 versus an accepted average of 6. That low early standing added further risk and reinforced the concern that your record did not show sufficient upward movement.

Next, ask admissions for a reconsideration meeting and request any feedback available. Focus on explaining or remedying your class rank: take additional rigorous courses if permitted, document improvement, and seek academic support. Your LSAT is a strength, so use it to show readiness, but the clearest path is to demonstrate stronger sustained academic performance and provide an updated record or verified improvement plan.
